All-New Mercedes-Benz C-Class Electric Arrives in the Land Down Under, Kicks Off at AU$105,700
16 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
The compact premium executive all-electric revolution has reached Australia as far as Mercedes-Benz is concerned, and this is the starting price for the all-new, first-ever Mercedes-Benz C-Class Electric – the C 400 4Matic version, that is.
Mercedes-Benz has been making the C-Class since 1993, when it was introduced as the replacement for the 190 model, and it’s been around for five generations before the premium German automaker decided to also make a battery electric compact executive car with the same name. The Mercedes-Benz C-Class Electric was initially teased during the 2025 Munich Motor Show launch event for the Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric cousin, and debuted in April 2026 in a single version, the C 400 4Matic.
The combustion version, by the way, is still around, and the W206 iteration introduced in early 2021 also got a mid-cycle refresh procedure in August 2026 to bring it up to snuff with the rest of the range and the Electric variant. Now the latter is going on sale in Australia, starting on October 20, 2026, in the same version as in other regions – the C 400 4Matic .
It “brings together expressive design, exhilarating electric performance and an immersive digital interior, while retaining the comfort and everyday usability that have long been the hallmark of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class.” Designed from scratch as an all-electric automobile, the C-Class Electric has the new visual identity of EVs for the brand, with the grille featuring 1,050 illuminated dots, an integrated central star and an illuminated surround.
There are animated lighting sequences for the grille, along with the three-pointed star LED daytime running lamps and the double-circle LED star taillights. In Australia, the AMG Line and the Night Package are standard, complete with 20-inch AMG multi-spoke light-alloy wheels. Inside, the AMG Line continues the theme, and there’s also the Keyless-go Convenience Package among other perks.
The cockpit has the latest Mercedes-Benz Operating System (MB.OS) connected to the Mercedes-Benz Intelligent Cloud, and features the fourth generation of MBUX, an AI-powered MBUX Virtual Assistant that combines technology from ChatGPT, Microsoft Bing and Google Gemini to understand natural speech, plus Mercedes-Benz Navigation with Electric Intelligence.
The MBUX Superscreen comes standard, featuring a 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster, a 14-inch central touchscreen and a dedicated 14-inch front-passenger display under the same glass surface, and buyers also get the standard AMG Line Sports Seat Package or a Burmester 3D surround sound system, among other things. All for AU$105,700, which equates to about $73,850 at the current exchange rate.
The powertrain uses a dual-motor electric drivetrain setup with 360 kW and 800 Nm, which is 483 hp and 590 lb-ft of torque, plus 4Matic all-wheel drive for a sprint to 100 kph or 62 mph in exactly four seconds. There’s a 94 kWh usable lithium-ion battery pack with a WLTP rating of up to 753 km (468 miles) of range, and the 800-volt platform enables DC fast charging at up to 330 kW.
